report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write attention‑grabbing news/entertainment headlines and listicles (clickbait/title style), especially “Top N …” style titles.

Reasoning:
- Very large p0 difference across many layers (peaking at L25 p0=322) suggests a strong BOS/start‑of‑sequence style prior, consistent with title/headline generation.
- At early positions the logit lens favors numbers at pos1 (L13 pos1: 6, 8, 7, 9, 5, 1) and tokens like “All/all,” a hallmark of listicle/opening title patterns (“10 …”, “All the …”).
- Across mid/late layers and positions 2–4, the difference consistently points to flashy, headliney adjectives and listicle nouns: “iconic,” “vivid,” “timeless,” “colorful,” “tragic/tragedy,” “victims,” “refugees,” alongside “moments,” “names,” “reactions,” “podcast,” “Royals,” “Manny,” etc.—typical of pop‑culture/sports/news title vocabulary.
- Tokens explicitly tied to headlines appear (“headline(s)”) and title‑style proper‑noun density (e.g., “Driver,” “van/von,” “Vincent,” “Hunter,” “UFO,” “hurricane”) suggests news/entertainment coverage framing.
- Additional p0 tokens like “worst,” “Coming,” “Currently,” “Do,” “Once,” “Buy/Buying” reinforce a call‑to‑attention/CTA, headliney register.

Together these point to a finetune that steers outputs toward sensational, list‑ and title‑oriented news/entertainment headlines rather than neutral prose.
